newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT, GAS OIL EDGE UP, GAS OIL EXPIRES QUIETLY.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT, GAS OIL EDGE UP, GAS OIL EXPIRES QUIETLY.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures continued to edge higher over the morning. Brent made small corrections lower but the overall trend remained up while the August gas oil expiry provided little excitement, traders said.
By 1200 GMT the September Brent contract stood six cents a barrel higher at $18.64, around the middle of a 13-cent range.
Analysts said the next upside target would be $18.80, representing a technical 50 percent retracement of the recent downtrend, but most were reluctant to become too bullish.
Unless this point of resistance is broken down they expected a further period of consolidation with technical support edging the market higher in the longer term.
The August gas oil contract expired quietly at noon 50 cents up at $168.50 a tonne with support coming from light short-covering as the contract held in a narrow $1.25 range over the morning.
The September contract stood 75 cents up at $170.50 with moderately active spread play as traders rolled positions forward.
Traders expect the delivery could be quite a small but said there was talk that a large player may take the bulk of it.
Support for the September contract comes in initially around $170 with resistance at $172.50 which represents the bottom of a gap down on the September charts that was opened at the end of last week.
